I was digging in my freezer and found some stewed strawberries so, after the ginger beer success, I decided to go for a strawberry pop.

While the strawberries were already in a syrup (425ml tub), I found them not sweet enough after I heated them with about 500ml water. I added 2 cups of sugar and about 2tbsp of ground ginger. I also added about 2-3tbsp of lemon juice for acidity.

Once the strawberries came nearly to a boil, I strained them through some cheesecloth into 1.5l cold water.

The brewing yeast I bought is garbage so I ended up pitching yeast twice into this ferment, like I had to do with the ginger beer. Despite adequate temperature and mild activity after proofing the yeast, 24 hours in the fermenter showed no significant bubbling. If the yeast doesn't take this time I'll either use bread yeast or drink it as juice.

One more thing, I wouldn't recommend using brewing yeast for this; it makes for a yeasty taste in the pop. I have heard champagne yeast is much better and I will be trying that next. Also, I want to try a brew with a ginger bug (like a sourdough but with ginger & sugar) as the bacteria and yeast simultaneously produce carbonation and acidity, which should make for a better tasting pop.
